chapter_intro: Jeremiah’s Struggles with God and Judah.

passages.title: Jeremiah’s Struggles with God and Judah.
passages.text: As the nation faces invasion, Jeremiah struggles to serve God faithfully. He is surprised by opposition (11:1–12:17), stunned over feeling betrayed by God (13:1–15:21), renewed by God (16:1–17:18), burdened by opposition (17:19–18:23), and prepared to continue serving (19:1–20:18).

notes.text: This is the first of several symbolic acts Jeremiah performs to reveal God’s will.
God orders Jeremiah to place underclothing in a rocky place. Of course, it gets ruined by the weather.
The Judeans’ prideful, idolatrous ways cling to them like an undergarment. Like Jeremiah’s garment, this pride will be ruined.
be not proud. Jeremiah urges Judah to repent. darkness. A common ancient Near Eastern symbol of judgment. my eyes will weep. Once again, Jeremiah expresses grief (compare 4:19–21; 9:1).
Negeb. Lands south of Jerusalem. shut up. They are awaiting or experiencing the Babylonian siege. If these cities are threatened, Jerusalem has already fallen.
flock. Judah’s people. friends. Babylon was once Judah’s ally (Isa. 39:1–8).
skirts . . . shame. Judah’s spiritual adultery will be exposed (Lam. 1:9). lewd whorings. See Ezek. 16:1–58; 23:1–48. Woe. Coming judgment (Isa. 5:8–23).
